events.title: AIP instructions clarify that only the funds needed to reach the threshold must be invested
events.description: Amended BN3 (effective 23 June 2024): after the first transfer, the principal applicant must transfer 'the remainder of the funds required to meet the minimum investment threshold (NZ$15 million or weighted equivalent)' into holding and/or acceptable investments; the 2022 text required the remainder of all nominated funds.
events.quote: the principal applicant has transferred the remainder of the funds required to meet the minimum investment threshold (NZ$15 million or weighted equivalent)

events.title: Border exception for Investor 1 investors approved in principle
events.description: The Cabinet Economic Development Committee agrees a border exception (during the COVID border closure) for Investor 1 resident visa holders and applicants approved in principle; 67 investors were eligible at the time and demand was expected to stay within about 100 investors.
events.quote: agreed to create a border exception to enable Investor 1 resident visa holders and applicants who have been approved-in-principle for an Investor 1 resident visa to be eligible to enter New Zealand

events.title: Investor migrant attraction and aftercare moved from INZ to NZTE
events.description: Joint Ministers transfer investor migrant attraction and aftercare services from Immigration New Zealand to New Zealand Trade and Enterprise from the start of the 2022/23 financial year; NZTE also becomes steward of which investments are acceptable for Active Investor Plus.
events.quote: to transfer the location of investor migrant attraction and aftercare services from INZ to NZTE from the beginning of the 2022/23 financial year

events.title: Cabinet agrees Growth ($5m) and Balanced ($10m) categories for Active Investor Plus
events.description: Cabinet decision (minute of 4 December 2024, CAB-24-MIN-ECO-0290 as listed on the coversheet) on the Minister of Immigration's paper: replace the weighting system with a Growth category ($5 million, three years, 21 days in NZ) and a Balanced category ($10 million, five years, 105 days, bonds and property allowed), six months to transfer and invest, no English requirement; go-live planned for end of February 2025 (implemented 1 April 2025).
events.quote: introduce two simplified investment pathways under the AIP visa that require applicants to choose from either ‘Growth’ ($5 million minimum investment) or ‘Balanced’ ($10 million minimum investment) categories

events.title: Discretionary Investment Management Services removed as an acceptable AIP investment
events.description: Discretionary Investment Management Services (DIMS) stop being an acceptable Growth category investment on 5 December 2025; $251.5 million had been invested through them.
events.quote: prior to their removal as an acceptable investment on 5 December 2025

events.title: Cabinet committee agrees philanthropy (up to 20%) in the AIP Growth category
events.description: Cabinet Economic Policy Committee minute ECO-26-MIN-0077 (13 May 2026) on the Minister's paper: Growth category applicants may make philanthropic gifts capped at 20 per cent of the total sum invested, to New Zealand-registered Tier 1-3 charities with five years of compliant returns, for domestic causes, with disclosure of affiliations; go-live planned for June 2026. A second, redacted investment class was also proposed.
events.quote: enable AIP Growth category applicants to make philanthropic gifts as part of their acceptable investment in New Zealand, capped at 20 per cent of the total sum invested

ledger.contains: INZ Operational Manual, archived BJ3 Investor 1 Category (effective 10/11/2016, 'to 28/07/2022'): requirements (health and character, NZ$10 million nominated and invested for three years, legally earned funds, fit and proper person). Rules added: investment amount and three-year investment period. No statistics.

INZ Operational Manual BJ5.45 Settlement funds (effective 27/07/2009; manual edition ceased 29 Nov 2010): Investor 2 principal applicants must show NZ$1 million settlement funds on top of the investment (already in the data as a rule), rules on joint ownership and evidence. Added the four-year investment period it mentions. No statistics.

Archived BJ5.45 Settlement funds (effective 29/11/2010, ceasing 22 May 2017): NZ$1 million settlement funds for Investor 2 and the note that the rule ends on 22 May 2017 (that change is already an event, from nzl-inz-ops-bj2-5-2017). Added the rule row for this version. No statistics.

INZ Operational Manual BJ8.15 (effective 27/07/2009): minimum time in New Zealand during the investment period, Investor 1 73 days a year, Investor 2 146 days a year. Both added as rules. No statistics.

Archived BJ8.15 (effective 28/08/2017, to 28/07/2022): final minimum-time rules, Investor 1 44 days in each of the last two years or 88 days with NZ$2.5m in growth investments; Investor 2 146 days in each of the last three years or 438 days with NZ$750,000 in growth investments. All four added as rules; earlier versions are only listed by date. No statistics.

Archived BN3 Active Investor Plus requirements (effective 19/09/2022): NZ$15 million or weighted equivalent, English, fit and proper, decline below NZ$5 million (both already in the data as rules), and the minimum first transfers before approval (NZ$1m listed equities/philanthropy, NZ$500,000 managed funds or NZ$100,000 direct investments), added as three rules. No statistics.

Archived BN3 Active Investor Plus requirements as amended 23/06/2024: same thresholds as 2022 (NZ$15m weighted, NZ$5m floor, first transfers NZ$1m/500,000/100,000), with the remainder now limited to the funds needed to reach the threshold. Added the rules for this version and a dated rule-change event. No statistics.

Earlier edition (5 March 2024, decisions 1 Jul 2013 to 29 Feb 2024) of the same INZ report, 100 pages: criteria by financial year 2013/14-2023/24 (applications p. 3, people p. 6), current year by month 2023-07 to 2024-02 (pp. 10-11), all criteria by nationality and year (pp. 13-36), nationality by substream (pp. 37-100, printed twice). Extracted every cell of the Investor 1, Investor 2 and Active Investor Plus rows (all years incl. 2016/17-2023/24, which this pass adds as this edition's own figures; some differ from the 2026 edition, e.g. Investor 2 approvals 2016/17 401 vs 400, 2019/20 105 vs 107, 2020/21 35 vs 36), the period totals, the eight months, and the 'Investor Category' nationality column (Investor 1, 2 and AIP combined; total 3,747 applications / 12,046 people, equal to the sum of the three criteria rows). '.' cells (no decisions) are not rowed. Duplicate sorted copies (pp. 69-100) checked identical; month-table totals equal FY2023/24. Everything adds up. Out of scope: other criteria.
